title: Blood plasma from people living with HIV-1 or HIV-2
projectDescription: In this study we performed data-independet mass-spectrometry analysis of blood plasma collected from a cohort consisting of people living with HIV-1, people living with HIV-2, and HIV seronegative individuals. The data was used to infer signs of damage to a wide array of tissues and cell types.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Prior to the sample preparation for the nano-scale liquid chromatographic tandem mass spectrometry (nLC-MS/MS) analysis, the 14 most abundant proteins (Albumin, alpha-1-acid glycoprotein, alpha-1-antitrypsin, alpha-2-macroglobulin, apolipoprotein A1, fibrinogen, haptoglobin, and transferrin, and the kappa and lambda light chains of immunoglobulin (Ig) G, IgA, IgM, IgD, and IgE) were depleted from four microlitre plasma using the High Select™ Top14 Abundant Protein Depletion Mini Spin Columns. The depleted samples were thereafter prepared using a filter-aided sample preparation (FASP) approach. One µg of sequencing Grade Modified Trypsin (Promega) was added to 30 µg protein, and the samples were digested at 37°C for 16 hours.  One µg of peptide solution per sample were injected onto the nLC column. The nLC-MS/MS analysis was performed on a Dionex Ultimate 3000 Rapid Separation LC nano Ultra-performance LC system coupled to an Orbitrap Exploris 480 MS with FAIMS Pro interface (Thermo Scientific). Peptides were loaded onto an Acclaim PepMap 100 C18 trap column and separated on an Easy-spray PepMap RSLC C18 column.  Full MS resolution was set to 120000 (at 200 m/z), AGC target value was 300% with a maximum injection time (IT) of 45 ms. Full MS mass range was set to m/z 380-1100. MS2 scans were acquired with a resolution of 30000 (at 200 m/z), fragmentation with a normalized collision energy (NCE) of 32, AGC target value was set to 1000% with automatic IT. Twenty-six variable isolation windows of 35.0, 22.5, 35.0 and 50.0 Da were used with an overlap of 0.5 Da, and with 1, 20, 1, 4 loop counts, respectively. For FAIMS, two compensation voltages (CVs) of -45 and -60 V were used with a carrier gas flow of 3.5 L/min and the spray voltage was set to 2.1 kV.
dataProcessingProtocol: The protein abundance was determined from peptide precursor and fragment ion intensities using the iq R-package. The protein intensity data was thereafter normalised by the variance stabilizing normalization (VSN) algorithm using the vsn R-package (v3.66.0). Based on data from GTEx and Human protein atlas databases, information regarding potential route of release to blood, tissue and cell type enhancement were assigned to the proteins. Z-scores were calculated for all proteins found to be enriched for a certain tissue or cell type.
